topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces her background, course themes, and the core learning outcomes on cancer etiology and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: The Biological Nature of Cancer and Sources of Oncogenic Mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as an evolutionary genetic process and describe the interplay of endogenous errors, heredity, and external mutagens.

topics.label: Epidemiological and Environmental Evidence for Cancer Causes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine environmental exposures, geographic and migrant epidemiology, and the debate regarding intrinsic luck versus environmental causation.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, illustrated in detail by the epidemiology and molecular etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical, Dietary, and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular pathways and metabolic activations through which specific dietary, radiation, and chemical exposures damage cellular DNA.

topics.label: Tumor Promoters and the Two-Stage Carcinogenesis Model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how non-mutagenic stimuli promote tumor outgrowth through chronic inflammation, receptor signaling, and sustained cellular proliferation.

topics.label: Host Susceptibility Factors and Summary of Carcinogenic Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how developmental life stages and tissue specificity modulate carcinogen susceptibility, accompanied by a synthesis of carcinogenic modes.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the experimental and observational methodologies used to establish carcinogenic potential, from mutational signatures to in vivo and in vitro assays.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture concludes by balancing practical risk-benefit trade-offs of environmental exposures alongside the key principles of carcinogenicity.
